newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mostly weaker, but fuel oil holds.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mostly weaker, but fuel oil holds.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mostly weaker with crude on Monday, except fuel oil which held its ground on strong fundamentals, traders said.

One seller of high sulphur fuel oil said he had four buyers for his cargo, all bidding fixed prices up to $110 fob Med for poor quality cracked material. "They are all pushing down the market to get some length and then ramp it up in early December," the seller said.
Low sulphur markets were steady, but near all-time highs as Italy bought heavily last week.
News that a new oil-fired power station in Brindisi, Italy is due to come on stream in early December merely confirmed traders' already bullish outlook.
Traders thought Italy was unlikely to buy more cargoes for Dec because congestion in Italian ports had already created delays of up to three weeks.

Gas oil prices slid $4.25 on lower IPE futures and heating oil premiums, offered around cif high +2 basis Genoa, under pressure from good supply. Availability includes a Russian export grade offered last week at cif high +$3 and an Italian grade cargo loading in late November.

Buying interest was seen in Greece at cif high -$1/1.50. Up to three other Russians loading before December remain unsold, with the owner maintaining they can be accommodated in his downstream system.

Naphtha cargoes fell $2 to $223/$225 cif. Traders said the Med looked balanced but recent delays at Algeria's Skikda and cargoes heading to the U.S., including Greek, Suez and Skikda, were underpinning prices.
Egypt's tender results for 1997 were seen this week with rumours of a $6.50-$7 premium to fob mean Med.
